successCriteria.description: src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts exposes a LeaveService with create, approve, reject, and cancel operations, each returning the persisted LeaveRequest.
create persists a request with status PENDING immediately (no DRAFT/SUBMITTED), validates startDate <= endDate, and rejects a request whose leaveType has no ACTIVE LeavePolicy with a typed error.
approve only transitions a PENDING request, denies self-approval (approver id === applicant id), and atomically updates status + commits balance + writes an APPROVE audit record.

approve computes the day count once via countLeaveDays and uses that same value for both the balance-sufficiency check and the balance deduction; an approval that would drive remainingDays below zero is rejected (InsufficientBalanceError), never clamped.
approve attributes the whole request to the fiscal year of startDate (calendar UTC year) and debits exactly one LeaveBalance row via commitDays keyed by (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear).
reject only transitions a PENDING request, denies self-rejection, and writes a REJECT audit record; cancel only transitions a PENDING request (owner-only) and writes an audit record.
every state-changing operation (create/approve/reject/cancel) writes exactly one AuditLog record with the matching AuditAction (CREATE/APPROVE/REJECT).

a shared pure helper fiscalYearOf(date): number is added beside countLeaveDays in src/shared/leave and exported from src/shared/leave/index.ts, deriving the UTC calendar year; no call site inlines date.getFullYear().

constraints: The service owns the transaction boundary and receives IUnitOfWork via constructor injection; it never imports the pg pool, a PoolClient, or any module-level db helper directly. Participating repository/service methods are called with the unit-of-work client as the optional last parameter.
The approve/reject flow (status update + balance commit + audit record) must be atomic: all three succeed or all three roll back.
All database access goes through repository interfaces (GP-001); the service never issues SQL or queries the employees/leave_balances/leave_policies tables directly.

The service enforces the business rule that a manager may not approve/reject their own request; RBAC role checks remain at the route boundary (requireRole) and are not re-implemented inline in the service.
The service imports sibling modules only through their public entry points (index.ts); no cross-module internal imports.
No `any`; use `unknown` with type guards. Strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks).
Deliverable is src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts only (plus the fiscalYearOf helper in src/shared/leave); no separate leave.service.interface.ts, no controller, no routes, no tests.
outOfScope: Unit/integration tests for the leave module (Phase 8c) — do not create test files or require test coverage.
Leave controller and routes (Phase 9), including API-boundary validation, requireRole wiring, and HTTP error mapping.
Leave domain model and repository (Phase 8a) — leave.model.ts and leave.repository.ts are owned by a sibling sub-phase.
Notification fanout / background jobs (no BullMQ) and any fiscal-calendar configuration field or per-policy fiscal calendar.

ambiguities.description: No concrete IUnitOfWork implementation exists anywhere in src/ (only the interface). LeaveService must receive IUnitOfWork via constructor, but this phase cannot reference a concrete class that does not exist — how the concrete implementation is supplied (injected by a later phase vs. constructed here) is unresolved.
options: Inject IUnitOfWork via constructor with no default; the controller/DI (Phase 9) supplies the concrete implementation
Inject IUnitOfWork via constructor with a default concrete implementation created in this phase
LeaveService accepts an optional IUnitOfWork and falls back to a non-transactional path when absent

entityInvariants.invariant: A request is created as PENDING immediately; the only legal transitions are PENDING→APPROVED, PENDING→REJECTED, and PENDING→CANCELLED (owner only); APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED are terminal and must never be re-transitioned.
startDate <= endDate always holds for a persisted request; a request may only be created against an ACTIVE LeavePolicy whose leaveType matches the request's leaveType.

Approving a request debits exactly one LeaveBalance row keyed by (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear) where fiscalYear is the calendar UTC year of startDate; remainingDays must never go below zero (reject, never clamp).
Every state-changing operation (create/approve/reject/cancel) produces exactly one AuditLog record with the matching AuditAction (CREATE/APPROVE/REJECT).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects invalid input (startDate > endDate, or no ACTIVE policy for the leaveType) with a typed error; persists status PENDING and writes a CREATE audit record.
Only from PENDING; denies self-approval; rejects (never clamps) when the balance would go below zero (InsufficientBalanceError); atomic status+balance+audit.
Only from PENDING; denies self-rejection; writes a REJECT audit record; no balance mutation.
Only from PENDING and only by the owner; writes an audit record; no balance mutation.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Use countLeaveDays(startDate, endDate) as the single source of the day count for BOTH the balance-sufficiency check and the balance deduction; never compute the day count independently.

Derive fiscalYear via the shared fiscalYearOf(date) helper (calendar UTC year of startDate) at every site that needs it — the balance-sufficiency check, the balance debit, and any findByEmployeeAndFiscalYear lookup — never inline date.getFullYear().

Debit the balance via commitDays(employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear, days, client), which atomically increments used_days and decrements remaining_days guarded by remaining_days >= days and throws InsufficientBalanceError on failure.
Resolve the LeavePolicy by leaveType via the policy module and filter to isActive policies itself, then use policy.id as the policyId for balance operations.

Enforce self-approval denial using isSubordinate(manager, applicantId, applicantManagerId), which returns false when applicantId === manager.id; read applicantManagerId from the employee module, never a direct employees-table query.
Write audit records via the audit module's record operation with AuditAction CREATE/APPROVE/REJECT, passing the unit-of-work client as the optional last parameter.
Receive IUnitOfWork via constructor and drive begin/commit/rollback with the exposed client; never import the pg pool or a PoolClient directly.
Use the LeaveType/LeaveStatus/AuditAction enums from the shared types module; do not re-declare them.

integrationPoints.why: create/updateStatus/findById for persisting requests and status transitions within the service's unit of work.
Balance-sufficiency check and atomic balance debit on approval.
Resolve the ACTIVE LeavePolicy for the request's leaveType to obtain policyId.
Read the applicant's managerId for the self-approval/subordination check.
Write CREATE/APPROVE/REJECT audit records for every state-changing operation.
Transaction boundary owned by the service; supplies the client passed to participating repositories.
